title: School voucher program on student test scores

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
The most suitable causal method for this research scenario is the Difference-in-Differences (DID) approach. This method is chosen because it allows us to compare the difference in outcomes (standardized test scores) between the treatment group (school districts with the voucher program) and the control group (school districts without the voucher program) before and after the introduction of the voucher program. The key assumption for DID to be valid is the parallel trends assumption, which states that the trends in the outcomes for the treatment and control groups would have been the same in the absence of the treatment. This assumption is testable by examining the pre-treatment trends in the data.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(readr)
library(plm)
librarytidyverse)

# Read the CSV file
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s03_data.csv")

# Convert data to panel data format
pdata <- pdata.frame(data, index = c("unit_id", "period"))

# Run the DID analysis
did_model <- plm(y ~ treat_x_post, data = pdata, model = "random", index = c("unit_id", "period"))

# Print the coefficient of the interaction term
summary(did_model)

# Basic robustness checks
# Test for parallel trends assumption
pre_trends <- plm(y ~ treated + post + treated:post, data = pdata, model = "random", index = c("unit_id", "period"))
summary(pre_trends)
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect the coefficient of the interaction term (`treat_x_post`) to be positive and statistically significant if the introduction of the school voucher program improves standardized test scores for students in treated school districts compared to control districts. The magnitude of the coefficient will indicate the average treatment effect of the voucher program on test scores. A positive coefficient would suggest that the voucher program has a positive effect on test scores, while a negative coefficient would indicate a negative effect. The significance level will provide evidence on whether the observed effect is due to chance or if it is a statistically significant result.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=voucher districts, control=non-voucher; shock=program introduction
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Test scores increase significantly in voucher districts after program launch
